title: Move Zeroes
interviewTips: Ask if solution must be in-place with O(1) extra space and if relative order of non-zero elements must be preserved.
Trade-off: extra array is simplest but uses O(n) space, two-pass overwrite plus zero-fill is O(1) space, single-pass swap is O(1) space with minimal operations and one traversal.
Check edge cases: empty array, single element, all zeros, no zeros, and cases like [0,1] and [1,0] to verify stability.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Extra Array Copy
approaches.intuition: Filter out non-zeros preserving order into a new array, then copy them back to front and fill rest with zeros.
approaches.theory: Stability comes from iterating left to right and appending only non-zeros. Rewriting the original array with that filtered list followed by zeros yields correct result. Uses extra storage proportional to input.

timeComplexity.explanation: One pass to filter non-zeros plus one pass to rewrite array, each linear.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Extra array holds up to n non-zero elements in worst case with no zeros.

edgeCases: All zeros -> tmp empty, entire array filled with zeros

approaches.name: Approach 2: Two-Pass In-Place Compaction
approaches.intuition: Compact all non-zeros to front in place using a write pointer, then fill tail with zeros.
approaches.theory: Maintain insertPos as next position for a non-zero. Reading left to right preserves order. Since insertPos never overtakes read index, overwrites are safe. Second pass fills remaining slots with zeros to complete partition.

timeComplexity.explanation: First pass compacts non-zeros, second pass fills zeros, total 2n operations worst case.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only insertPos pointer used, in-place modification.

edgeCases: All zeros -> insertPos stays 0, whole array zeroed
Already partitioned [1,2,0,0] -> second pass only rewrites zeros
Large array with one non-zero still O(n)

approaches.name: Approach 3: Single-Pass Swap with Slow-Fast Pointers
approaches.intuition: Use slow pointer for last non-zero boundary and fast pointer to scan, swapping each non-zero forward only when needed.
approaches.theory: Invariant: elements before lastNonZero are non-zeros in original order, elements between lastNonZero and i are zeros. When nums[i] is non-zero, swapping with lastNonZero extends non-zero prefix by one. Self-swap when i equals lastNonZero is harmless and can be skipped. Single traversal maintains stability.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single linear scan with O(1) swap per non-zero element.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two indices used, all swaps in place.

edgeCases: No zeros -> only self-swaps, array unchanged
